title: Pandas
label: Pandas
desc: Python library for labeled tabular data and time series analysis.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install pandas and import it under the usual alias:

snippets.code:
# From PyPI
pip install pandas

# With conda
conda install -c conda-forge pandas

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

print(pd.__version__)

sections.title: Series
sections.description: Create and inspect one-dimensional labeled arrays:

snippets.code:
s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30], index=["a", "b", "c"], name="score")

s["b"]        # 20 by label
s.iloc[0]      # 10 by position
s.values       # array([10, 20, 30])
s.index        # Index(['a', 'b', 'c'], dtype='object')
s.mean()       # 20.0
s + 5          # element-wise addition

s = pd.Series({"a": 10, "b": 20, "c": 30})

s > 15                  # boolean mask
s[s > 15]               # labels b and c
s.map({10: "low", 20: "mid", 30: "high"})
s.value_counts()
s.sort_values(ascending=False)

sections.title: DataFrame
sections.description: Build a table from columns and inspect its structure:

snippets.code:
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Ana", "Bob", "Cid"],
    "age": [31, 24, 45],
    "city": ["Recife", "Lisboa", "Recife"],
})

df.head(2)
df.shape            # (3, 3)
df.columns.tolist() # ['name', 'age', 'city']
df.dtypes
df.info()
df.describe()

df["active"] = True
df["age_next"] = df["age"] + 1

renamed = df.rename(columns={"city": "town"})
dropped = df.drop(columns=["active"])
indexed = df.set_index("name")
flat = indexed.reset_index()

sections.title: Reading Data
sections.description: Load CSV files with common parsing options:

snippets.code:
df = pd.read_csv("sales.csv")

df = pd.read_csv(
    "sales.csv",
    sep=";",
    header=0,
    index_col="id",
    dtype={"zip": str},
    parse_dates=["order_date"],
)

# Only two columns and the first 500 rows
df = pd.read_csv("sales.csv", usecols=["id", "total"], nrows=500)

# Treat these tokens as missing values
df = pd.read_csv("sales.csv", na_values=["NA", "-", ""])

df = pd.read_excel("report.xlsx", sheet_name="Q1")
df = pd.read_json("events.json", lines=True)
df = pd.read_parquet("orders.parquet", columns=["id", "total"])
df = pd.read_sql("SELECT id, total FROM orders", con=engine)

sections.title: Selecting
sections.description: Pick columns, rows and single cells by label or position:

snippets.code:
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {"name": ["Ana", "Bob", "Cid"], "age": [31, 24, 45], "city": ["Recife", "Lisboa", "Recife"]},
    index=["a", "b", "c"],
)

df["age"]                # one column as Series
df[["name", "city"]]     # two columns as DataFrame
df.loc["b", "age"]       # 24 by label
df.loc["a":"b", "name"]  # label slice, end included
df.iloc[0, 1]            # 31 by position
df.iloc[0:2, 0:2]        # first two rows and columns
df.at["c", "city"]       # fast scalar by label
df.iat[2, 2]             # fast scalar by position

sections.title: Filtering
sections.description: Keep rows that satisfy boolean conditions:

snippets.code:
mask = (df["age"] >= 30) & (df["city"] == "Recife")
df[mask]

df[df["city"].isin(["Recife", "Lisboa"])]
df[df["age"].between(25, 40)]
df[df["name"].str.startswith("A")]
df[~df["city"].eq("Lisboa")]   # negation

limit = 30
df.query("age > @limit and city == 'Recife'")

sections.title: Sorting
sections.description: Order rows by values, index or magnitude:

snippets.code:
df.sort_values("age")
df.sort_values(["city", "age"], ascending=[True, False])
df.sort_values("age", ascending=False, na_position="first")
df.sort_index()
df.nlargest(2, "age")

sections.title: Grouping
sections.description: Split rows into groups and aggregate each one:

snippets.code:
df.groupby("city")["age"].mean()
df.groupby("city").size()

df.groupby("city").agg(
    people=("name", "count"),
    total_age=("age", "sum"),
    oldest=("age", "max"),
)

# Broadcast the group total back to every row
df["city_total"] = df.groupby("city")["age"].transform("sum")

df.groupby(["city", "name"])["age"].sum()
df.groupby("city")["age"].agg(["min", "mean", "max"]).round(1)

sections.title: Merging and Joining
sections.description: Combine tables by key or stack them vertically:

snippets.code:
users = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "name": ["Ana", "Bob", "Cid"]})
orders = pd.DataFrame({"user_id": [1, 1, 3], "total": [20.0, 35.5, 12.0]})

pd.merge(orders, users, left_on="user_id", right_on="id", how="left")
pd.merge(orders, users, left_on="user_id", right_on="id", how="inner", suffixes=("_order", "_user"))

pd.concat([users, users], ignore_index=True)

users.set_index("id").join(orders.set_index("user_id"), how="left")

sections.title: Pivot and Reshape
sections.description: Move between long and wide layouts:

snippets.code:
df.pivot_table(index="city", columns="name", values="age", aggfunc="mean")
df.pivot_table(index="city", values="age", aggfunc=["mean", "max"], fill_value=0)

wide = df.pivot(index="name", columns="city", values="age")
long = wide.reset_index().melt(id_vars="name", var_name="city", value_name="age")

stacked = wide.stack()   # Series with a MultiIndex
stacked.unstack()        # back to a DataFrame

sections.title: Missing Data
sections.description: Detect, drop and fill absent values:

snippets.code:
df.isna().sum()                  # missing count per column
df.dropna()                      # drop rows with any missing value
df.dropna(subset=["name"])       # require only the name column
df.dropna(axis=1, how="all")     # drop columns that are entirely empty

df.fillna(0)
df.fillna({"age": df["age"].mean(), "city": "unknown"})
df["age"].ffill()                # carry the last valid value forward
df["age"].interpolate()          # linear interpolation

sections.title: Dates and Time Series
sections.description: Parse timestamps and resample a time index:

snippets.code:
df["order_date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["order_date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")

pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=4, freq="W")

df["year"] = df["order_date"].dt.year
df["month"] = df["order_date"].dt.month_name()
df["weekday"] = df["order_date"].dt.day_name()

ts = df.set_index("order_date").sort_index()

ts.resample("W")["total"].sum()
ts["total"].rolling("7D").mean()
ts.loc["2024-01"]

df["ts"] = pd.to_datetime(df["ts"], utc=True)
df["ts"].dt.tz_convert("America/Sao_Paulo")

sections.title: Apply and Map
sections.description: Transform values with functions and mappings:

snippets.code:
df["name"].map(str.upper)
df["city"].map({"Recife": "BR", "Lisboa": "PT"})
df["age"].apply(lambda x: "senior" if x >= 40 else "junior")

# Row-wise function; axis=1 passes each row as a Series
df.apply(lambda row: row["age"] * 2, axis=1)

df.assign(age_next=df["age"] + 1)
df[["age"]].map(lambda x: x + 1)   # element-wise on a DataFrame

sections.title: Writing Data
sections.description: Save a DataFrame to disk or a database:

snippets.code:
df.to_csv("clean.csv", index=False)
df.to_csv("clean.csv", sep=";", columns=["name", "age"], na_rep="")
df.to_excel("report.xlsx", sheet_name="people", index=False)
df.to_parquet("people.parquet", engine="pyarrow", compression="snappy")
df.to_json("people.json", orient="records", indent=2)
df.to_sql("people", con=engine, if_exists="replace", index=False)
